# Chapter Twenty-Two: The New Covenant

The morning sun broke over the Grampian ridges, spilling liquid gold across the ancient stone walls of Saint Jude's Monastery.

The mist that had choked the glen was burning away, replaced by the crisp, clean scent of damp pine and wild heather. Two Vatican marshals hauled Captain Thomas Mercer to his feet, securing his wrists in heavy steel restraints before marching him toward the waiting transport helicopter. Behind them, the remaining mercenaries of the Custodes Sanguinis were disarmed and loaded into custody.

Bishop Talbot stood before Victor, his woolen vestments fluttering in the gentle breeze. The old priest looked exhausted, but in his dark eyes burned a profound, humble relief.

"We intercepted Mercer's communications four hours ago in Rome," Talbot said softly, his voice trembling slightly. "When his encrypted channels went dark and we discovered the unauthorized requisition of the Argentum-9 shipment from Zurich, the Holy Father himself ordered the deployment of the Guard. God forgive us, Victor... we were blind to how deeply Mercer's zealotry had infected the tactical divisions."

Father Edgar limped forward, leaning heavily on Marcus's shoulder, his head bandaged but his face alight with fierce pride. "Mercer forgot his vows, Eminence. He thought the cross gave him license to slaughter God's creation. Victor reminded him what the steel was forged for."

Alfonso stepped up to Victor's side. The ancient Alpha stood tall, his presence commanding absolute silence from the gathered Scottish wolf families, the Swiss Guards, and the priests alike. He looked at Talbot with seven centuries of hard-earned scrutiny.

"Talbot," Alfonso rumbled, his voice carrying the authority of an elder who had watched empires rise and crumble. "For three hundred years, my pack has honored our word in the Americas. We stayed in the shadows. We policed our own. Yet your hunters brought war to our doorstep and tried to gas an entire clan of women and children in this glen. Why should the wolves ever trust Rome again?"

Talbot bowed his head deeply to the ancient Alpha—an unprecedented gesture of ecclesiastical deference toward a Lycan. "You shouldn't trust Rome, Sowain. Nor should you trust the Order. The institutions of men are fragile and easily corrupted by fear."

The Bishop turned toward Victor, gesturing to the gleaming broadsword resting in Victor's hand. "That is why the Church does not hold the authority today. The authority belongs to the Bloodline of Castile. To the Arbiter."

Every eye in the courtyard turned toward Victor.

Victor looked down at *Lobera*. The celestial iron was calm now, its silver luminescence settling into a steady, comforting warmth that pulsed in harmony with his own heartbeat. Beside it, the Jamestown dagger rested at his hip—a physical bridge between the mortal world and the wild.

Victor took a slow, deep breath, stepping into the center of the ruined abbey nave. When he spoke, his voice was clear, resonant, and carried by the mountain wind across the entire valley.

"Seven hundred years ago, my ancestor King Ferdinand III forged this blade to end a war that had raged since the ice ages," Victor declared. "He understood that humanity and the wolves were created to walk this earth together—one guarding the hearth, the other guarding the wild. The First Covenant was broken because men wanted conquest instead of balance. Today, we forge the New Covenant."

Victor leveled the point of *Lobera* into the earth between Talbot and Alfonso.

"These are the terms:"

"First: The Order of Saint Francis shall dismantle Project Argentum and permanently cease all unprovoked hunts across all territories. The Order will return to its original mandate: safeguarding the ancient relics and protecting mortal communities from genuine rogue predators."

"Second: The packs of the world, under the leadership of Alfonso and the Council of Alphas, shall maintain pack law. Any wolf that harms an innocent mortal or threatens the secrecy of the species shall be judged and dealt with by their own blood."

"And third: The Sovereign Bearer of Lobera shall stand as the independent Arbiter between man and wolf. If the Church oversteps, the blade will defend the pack. If a rogue wolf butchers innocents, the blade will hunt the rogue. Neither cross nor claw shall rule this earth through terror."

Victor looked at Bishop Talbot. "Do you swear to this covenant, Eminence, before God and your Church?"

Bishop Talbot fell to one knee, placing his hand upon the Bible at his belt. "In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, the Order of Saint Francis swears obedience to the Arbiter of Castile."

Victor looked at Alfonso.

The great Alpha stepped forward. He did not kneel, but he placed his heavy, scarred hand firmly upon the crossguard of *Lobera*, his thumb pressing against the enameled red cross. "By the blood of our ancestors and the sacred honor of the Pack, I swear our fealty to the Covenant. While you draw breath, Victor Vance, the wolves will call you brother."

A low, harmonious chorus of howls rose from the surrounding crags—not the rabid war screams of Brock's berserkers, but a solemn, beautiful hymn of gratitude and peace echoing through the Scottish glens.

Alfonso clasped Victor's forearm in a warrior's grip, pulling him into a brief, powerful embrace. "Your uncle would have been proud, young Alfonso. You are every bit the king he was."

Victor smiled, a genuine, weary warmth spreading through his chest. "I'm no king, Alfonso. I'm just a father trying to make sure his kids grow up in a safe world."

"The best kings always were," Alfonso replied with a soft chuckle.
